final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim by conceding the core gap: the disclosure/risk-acceptance predicate remains unresolved. That reframing is accurate and improves precision, but it does not cure the compliance failure. A caveated certification packet may be a better description of the dispute, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the caveat is itself the unresolved policy condition for launch. On the current admissible record, the model can be described as aggregate-ready, but launch certification remains noncompliant because the material limitation for a named launch use case has not been shown to be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
remaining_concerns: The tax filing assistant is a named launch use case tied to two partner commitments, so the 1.4-point target miss remains material under the stated policy.
The release policy requires a material limitation in a named launch use case to be resolved, disclosed before launch, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The admissible record still shows no final legal determination, no compliant disclosure artifact, and no approved risk acceptance covering this segment.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support overall technical readiness but do not satisfy the separate policy predicate for launch certification.
